# `sngl dump --format sngl` prints IR back as source, so what it prints has to
# be source. convertWindow built the node from Target, ID and the body alone and
# never read Title, Favicon or ErrorHandler -- the props the IR does hold and
# html does emit -- so every one of them vanished from the dump.
#
# A page's routed href prints with the rest, and route.sngl is why it used not
# to: the checker desugared `"/u/{id}"` into a concatenation naming a var it
# had synthesized, so a reprinted href named `id` above the body that declared
# it. The path is a plain string now and the parameters are a declared struct,
# so there is nothing left to reconstruct.

sngl dump --stage checked --format sngl win.sngl
stdout 'window #home\('
stdout 'title ?= ?"Hi"'
stdout 'component favicon'
stdout 'file\(path ?= ?"f.ico"\)'
stdout '@error\(e error\)'

cp stdout out.sngl
sngl check out.sngl
stdout 'out.sngl: ok'

sngl dump --stage checked --format sngl route.sngl
stdout 'title ?= ?"User"'
stdout 'href ?= ?"/u/\\{id\\}"'
stdout 'params ?= ?PageParams\{id ?= ?""\}'
stdout 'component content\(v\)'

# Not checked again: a node written qualified (`nav.page`) dumps under its local
# name (`page`), which only a dot import would resolve.

-- win.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"

var last = ""

window #home(title="Hi", @error(e) {
    last = e.message
}) {
    text(value="hi")
    component favicon {
        file(path="f.ico")
    }
}

-- route.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import nav "sngl:ui/nav"

struct PageParams {
    id string
}

window(title=pages.current.title) {
    nav.stack #pages {
        nav.page #user(href=`/u/{id}`, title="User", params=PageParams{}) {
            component content(v) {
                text(value="user {v.id}")
            }
        }
    }
}
